lesson.title: The Real Secret to Faster Chord Changes

source.creator: Lauren Bateman
source.licensing: exercise-only, no song material — safe per spec §3/R6

lesson.one_line_promise: Why your chord changes are slow — and the 3 drills that fix it.
lesson.core_concept: Tension slows your hands. Speed comes from repetition that builds muscle memory, which is what lets you relax. You cannot rush the relaxation.
prerequisites: Can form Em, C, G, D open chords (even slowly)
objectives: Understand why chord changes feel hard (new motor pattern + tension)
Warm up hands with the spider exercise
Build finger independence with lift-off drills
Use a metronome as a scorecard for chord-change speed
Use pivot points to make Em-C and Em-G easier

free_metronome: EX3 uses built-in metronome — funnel front door
adaptive_loop: Raise target changes/min week over week from logged baseline

chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Spider exercise (finger dexterity warm-up)
exercises.purpose: Blood flow + fine-motor control + coordinate fretting and picking hands.

params.strings: 6 down to 1, then back up (low E -> high e -> low E)
params.tempo: very slow; count '1 2 3 4', advance to next note on each 1
params.breathing_cue: Breathe; don't hold breath (holding breath = tension = slow)

exercises.coaching: Keep fingers relaxed and close to the fretboard. They'll feel floppy at first — that floppy feeling IS the control you're building.
exercises.qa_status: QA-PENDING (confirm start fret 7 = least stretch; confirm 3 fingers not 4)

exercises.name: Finger lift-off / 'finger push-ups'
exercises.purpose: Finger independence + retain chord shape when lifting a finger.

params.action: Lift 3rd finger, then 2nd, then 1st, one at a time; rebuild. Progress to peeling all off and landing together.
params.air_variant: Lift hand off guitar, make shapes in air, drop back down.
params.duration_min: few minutes only (tendon caution — instructor notes tendinitis risk)

exercises.coaching: If your hand flattens when you let go, that's normal — muscle memory hasn't formed yet. Reps fix it.

exercises.name: 1-2 minute chord-change drill (metronome scorecard)
exercises.purpose: Measurable speed gain; psychological push past comfort tempo.

params.measure: count completed changes in the window
params.push_technique: Set tempo slightly ABOVE comfort, then return — makes comfort tempo feel slow.
params.clarity_rule: During speed push, muted strings are OK; goal is finger SPEED to target, clean up later.
params.slow_variant: 30s slow (clarity: fingers move together + hover) + 30s fast

exercises.coaching: Write the number down. That's your scorecard — next week, beat it. Speed first, clean second.
exercises.qa_status: QA-PENDING (baseline range is anecdotal, not validated)

common_mistakes: Learning too many chords at once — teach 4 at a time (G, Em, C, D = thousands of songs).
Going too fast too soon — slow builds muscle memory; push speed only inside drills.
Practicing songs instead of transitions — dedicate a block to chord changes specifically.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Slow chord changes aren't a talent problem — they're a muscle-memory problem. Today we warm up your hands and turn your metronome into a scorecard. Grab your guitar.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: First, the spider. Start at the 7th fret where it's least stretchy. One finger per fret — index, middle, ring. Three slow picks per string, top to bottom and back. Breathe. Floppy fingers are normal.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Now make a C shape and lift fingers one at a time. If your hand forgets the shape when you let go, that's expected. We're teaching your fingers where to go.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Here's the scorecard. Metronome on, Em to C, back and forth, for one minute. Count your changes. Don't worry about buzz — we're chasing speed. Write the number down.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: Your count this session is your baseline. Next session, beat it by one. That's how 16 becomes 30.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: You're never too old for this. Consistency beats talent. Three drills, five minutes, most days — that's the whole secret.
